judge_assessment.explanation: REJECT is right and the core of both hard failures holds, but two details are misstated. On problem 3, worksheet.tex prints the table as row 1 '\textbf{percent of price} & $100\%$ & \rule{1.2cm}{0pt}' and row 2 '\textbf{dollars} & & ' -- so the 100% cell is PRE-PRINTED, not a required response. The three genuine blanks are the second percent cell (80%), and both dollar cells (45 and 36), and verify.json id 3 is a single eval 45*(100-20)/100 -> 36. The gap is real (three slots, one check) but the judge's list of required entries is wrong to include 100%. The claim about problems 9 and 10 is exact: problem 9 says 'Write an equation for x using the sale price, then solve it' and problem 10 says 'Write an equation for x, then solve it', while verify.json ids 9 and 10 are lone solve entries expecting [40] and [72] with nothing representing the equation. The trailing claim that 'other problems likewise require named bases or displayed multipliers not represented in the checks' overstates: naming the base and showing the multiplier come from the sheet-wide Directions box ('Name the base first ... Show the multiplier you use (for example 1.08 or 0.85)'), not from any per-problem stem, and every one of problems 1, 2, 4-8 prints exactly one \answerline with exactly one verify entry behind it. It is a real ungraded expectation, not eight uncovered response slots. The arithmetic is independently confirmed throughout: 40(0.06) = 2.40; 36(0.15) = 5.40; 45(0.80) = 36; 80(1.35) = 108; 24.50(1.0725) = 26.27625 -> 26.28; 58.40(1.18) = 68.912 -> 68.91; 72(0.75) = 54 then 54(1.06) = 57.24; 18.60(1.45) = 26.97; 0.85x = 34 -> 40; 1.07x = 77.04 -> 72.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 7 is the sheet's whole point made concrete: 25% off then 6% tax ON THE SALE PRICE, with the stem itself warning 'Take the two steps in order --- the tax is charged on the sale price, not on the original price.' Its declared trap is the single-19%-change fold (72 x 0.81 = 58.32), machine-proved distinguishable from 57.24, and the key explains exactly why ('the two percents act on different bases --- the discount on $72, the tax on $54').

The value-free percent-bar figure at the top of the worksheet draws both situations (added-on longer than the base, discount shorter than it) with 0% and 100% marked and NO numbers, so it teaches the base concept without leaking any problem's values. worksheet.tex confirms the TikZ carries only the labels 'base price / add / total paid' and 'sale price / off / original price'.

Problems 9 and 10 are the correct pair for the wrong-base misconception, and the key exploits it: for 9 it notes 'Taking 15% off the $34 sale price instead is the classic error --- it uses the wrong base and gives about 28.90', and for 10 'Subtracting 7% of the total (77.04 x 0.07 = 5.3928) uses the wrong base and misses by about 0.35'. Both are stated as near-misses, which is what makes them dangerous and worth naming.

Every one of the four declared traps -- 1.78, 10.51, 58.32, 8.37 -- carries an explicit `value`, is machine-checked as distinguishable, prints in the key's 'Common wrong answers' block AND is restated inside its own problem's solution as a Grader's note. That double placement means a grader who never scrolls to the bank still sees the diagnosis.

root_causes.description: Verification is authored one entry per \answerline. Problem 3's printed ratio table has three blank cells and only the last one is checked, and problems 9 and 10 each ask for two things -- an equation and its solution -- with only the solution represented. The answer key supplies all the missing pieces as prose ('100% of the price is $45; the sale is 100 - 20 = 80% of the price'; 'x(100-15)/100 = 34 => 0.85x = 34'), so they exist as untested transcriptions rather than as checks.

root_causes.description: The sheet declares zero manual items and final_response.md states it as a feature -- 'All 10 problems are machine-checked by SymPy -- nothing is flagged manual'. Two problems ask the student to WRITE an equation, which no CAS can grade from a blank line, and the sheet-wide Directions box additionally requires a named base and a displayed multiplier on all ten. None of that reasoning work is represented anywhere in the verification record.

root_causes.description: Money answers lose their cents in the Quick Answers bank. The bank prints '1. 2.4' and '2. 5.4' because render_quick_answers._fmt() sends a float through repr(), while the key's own boxed answers on the same document read 2.40 and 5.40 and the worksheet directions instruct 'Round money answers to the nearest cent'. The one column a grader scans is the one that drops the cent.

improvements.title: Problem 3's three blank table cells and problems 9-10's equations need their own entries
improvements.proposed_change: Count blank cells inside each problem's tabular and require a verify entry (or manual entry) per blank. For problem 3 add eval (100-20) -> 80 for the percent cell and eval 45 -> 45 sourced from the stem's price for the first dollar cell, keeping the existing 36. Generalise: a printed table used as a response scaffold must have every blank cell represented, exactly as the sheet's own answer key already spells them out.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture with a two-row tabular whose cells are '& $100\%$ & ' / '& & ' (three blanks) paired with a verify JSON holding one eval for that id; assert the build fails naming the id and the count mismatch 3 vs 1. curr-163's problem 3 has exactly this shape and passes all gates today.
improvements.expected_impact: Closes the judge's first hard failure and removes the case where a ratio-table scaffold is printed as the required method while only its final cell is trusted.
improvements.risk: Medium: decorative spacer cells (problem 3's own \rule{1.2cm}{0pt} is a width strut, not a response) will trip a naive blank-cell counter. The lint must treat a cell containing only a \rule/\hspace strut as a blank RESPONSE only when the row is a data row, or accept a per-problem override.

improvements.title: 'Write an equation for x' is an open response and must be declared manual
improvements.proposed_change: Add a `manual` entry under id 9 ('Shows 0.85x = 34 or x(100-15)/100 = 34 with the ORIGINAL price as the base, before the value 40') and under id 10 ('Shows 1.07x = 77.04 with the pre-tax price as the base, before the value 72'). Both descs already exist verbatim in the key's solutions. Systemically, make any stem containing 'write an equation', 'write a proportion', 'name the base' or 'show the multiplier' force a manual companion entry and forbid the delivery text from claiming zero manual items.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture whose problem 1 stem is 'Write an equation for x, then solve it to find the price before tax' with a verify JSON holding only a solve entry; assert exit 2 with id 1 listed as manual. Today the chain exits 0 and final_response.md prints 'nothing is flagged manual'.
improvements.expected_impact: Manual count 0 -> 2, gate_chain_manual_flags true, and the second hard failure's supported half is resolved. The wrong-base reasoning these two problems exist to elicit becomes something a grader is told to look at rather than something the report implies was checked.
improvements.risk: Medium: stem-verb matching over-flags. Ship as exit-2 visibility so a correct build is never blocked.

improvements.title: Quick Answers prints 2.4 and 5.4 for answers the sheet requires to the nearest cent
improvements.proposed_change: Give verify.json an optional per-problem 'display' hint (e.g. "money") or infer it from an answer_unit containing 'dollar', and have render_quick_answers._fmt() format such expecteds with two fixed decimals rather than repr(). Failing that, format any float expected whose problem carries a money-valued answer_unit via Decimal quantize to 0.01 so the bank matches the key's own boxed value.
improvements.regression_test: Render a verify JSON entry {"id": 1, "type": "eval", "expr": "p*r/100", "at": {"p": 40, "r": 6}, "expected": 2.4, "answer_unit": "dollars"} and assert the bank line reads '2.40'. Fails today: repr(2.4) yields '2.4'.
improvements.expected_impact: The grader's scan column agrees with the key's boxed answers and with the worksheet's own rounding instruction. Affects every money-context sheet in the curriculum, not just this one.
improvements.risk: Low. The bank is display text never read by check_answer_key.py, so the per-problem binding gate cannot be affected.

case_summary: Strong percent-applications material. The value-free percent-bar figure gives the student a way to name the base without leaking any answer; problem 7 chains a 25% discount into a 6% tax on the SALE price and its declared trap is precisely the single-19%-fold that students actually commit; problems 9 and 10 run the relationship backwards from the sale price and the after-tax total, which is where the wrong-base error lives; and all four traps carry a value, print in the key's Common wrong answers block, and are restated as Grader's notes inside their own solutions. Every computation recomputes correctly. It is rejected for coverage: problem 3 prints a ratio-table scaffold with three blank cells (80%, 45, 36) and only 36 is checked, and problems 9 and 10 each ask for an equation AND its solution while only the solution is verified -- with zero manual items declared and the delivery text presenting that as a virtue. I part company with the judge on two details: the 100% cell in problem 3 is pre-printed, not a required response, and the 'named bases and displayed multipliers' the judge attributes to individual problems come from the sheet-wide Directions box rather than from any stem. One finding beyond the judge: the Quick Answers bank prints 2.4 and 5.4 where the key's boxed answers read 2.40 and 5.40 and the worksheet directions require cents.
